subtype: Approach: rehearsing the request with a sibling [Thinking]
passage: Papa's scooter would be back in twenty minutes, so Iram pulled her older brother Samir into the front room. "You be Papa. I ask for the trip with my friends." Samir folded his arms and dropped his voice. "A day trip? Who is going? Who is driving? Why should I trust this?" "Everyone is going!" Iram said. Samir shook his head. "That is the weakest thing you can say." Iram groaned, then tried again: the names of the friends, two grown-ups coming, the bus timings, her phone in her pocket. Samir gave one stern nod. "Better." The scooter horn sounded early, and Iram wiped her palms on her kurta.

qa.q: Which argument did Samir call the weakest one?
qa.a: He called "Everyone is going!" the weakest thing Iram could say.

qa.q: What was Iram feeling when the scooter horn sounded early?
qa.a: Nervous, since she wiped her palms on her kurta as her practice time ran out. 😅

qa.q: What other way could Iram prepare, and why would it help?
qa.a: She could write down the plan with names, timings and the bus route to hand to her parents, because they can read it slowly and she will not forget details.

qa.q: How might Samir see his part as the strict father?
qa.a: He seems to take it seriously, giving real objections and a nod when the answers improved, so he probably wants Iram to succeed.

grounding: A girl practises a trip request on her older brother, who plays a strict father, and learns which arguments sound weak.
